Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our son complains that things look blurry to him. This has been an issue for a while now, and we're concerned it might affect his learning at nursery.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, he often asks us to repeat ourselves because he didn't quite catch what we said the first time. It's like he needs a little more time to process the sounds.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: The dentist mentioned his teeth have weak enamel. We're trying to take good care of them with regular brushing and dental visits to prevent further issues.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: He needs to go for regular heart check-ups due to a condition that was identified early on. The doctors keep a close eye on it to ensure everything stays under control.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone. It's something we're working with the physiotherapist to improve.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: He's very picky with food textures. Some foods he just won't eat because of how they feel in his mouth. We're trying to gradually introduce new textures to help him get used to variety.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: He has scoliosis, which we're managing with physical therapy and regular exercises to strengthen his back muscles.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a heart condition that requires regular check-ups to ensure everything stays under control.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is picky with food textures and has difficulty eating certain foods due to their texture, but there are no other reported gastrointestinal issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, which affects his muscle tone, and is working with a physiotherapist to improve it.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have other neurological issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties and often asks for repetition, indicating possible conductive hearing loss.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient complains of blurry vision, which may affect his learning.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on his teeth, which requires regular dental care to prevent further issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, people with KBG syndrome can have a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's vision and hearing difficulties may affect his learning at nursery.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and some may require special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has scoliosis, which is being managed with physical therapy and regular exercises.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some may have short fingers or other skeletal anomalies.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage the patient's weak enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to address the patient's hearing difficulties
* Eyesight review to assess and correct the patient's blurry vision
* Regular heart check-ups to monitor the patient's heart condition
* Physiotherapy to improve the patient's muscle tone and manage his scoliosis
* Occupational therapy to help the patient with feeding difficulties and food texture issues
* Speech therapy to address any speech delays or difficulties related to the patient's hearing loss
* Behavioural therapy to support the patient's behavioural development and any related issues

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hearing difficulties, often requiring repeated requests for her to respond.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has issues with food textures and can be picky, affecting her diet and potentially indicating gastrointestinal issues.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient had otitis media in the past and has been monitored for signs of it returning, indicating potential issues with her ears.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient sits close to the TV and holds books close to her face, suggesting potential vision problems.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an abnormality with his heart valve.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is very particular about food textures and some foods he won't touch because of how they feel.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired pretty easily when playing or running around and has low energy levels compared to other kids his age.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and some may have tethered cord, which can cause pain and weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is bothered by loud noises and gets frustrated when there's too much going on around him.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes squints, which makes his parent worry about his eyesight.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs to visit the dentist more often than most kids his age because of some problems they've found with his teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: As well as large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems developmentally behind where his parent thinks he should be compared to his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient seems developmentally behind where his parent thinks he should be compared to his peers.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may have developmental delay.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: One of the patient's testicles didn't descend properly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor the patient's teeth problems.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to check for any hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to assess the patient's vision and check for any vision problems.
* Cardiac review to monitor the patient's heart condition.
* Consider a skeletal review to check for any spinal or bone abnormalities.
* Consider physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and behaviour.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences faster breathing than expected when playing actively.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's breathing gets faster than expected when playing actively, but doctors have checked her out and everything seems okay.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, and the parents try to ensure she drinks enough water and eats fiber-rich foods to help with that.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, and the parents work closely with her neurologist to manage them.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient sometimes asks her parents to repeat things because she didn't quite catch what they said the first time.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypermetropia and needs glasses to see clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel, and the parents make sure to brush her teeth regularly and limit sugary snacks.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including weak enamel and large front teeth.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and many go to mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences, such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient stands and walks with a noticeably different posture, and the doctors mentioned hip dysplasia as something they're keeping an eye on.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor weak enamel
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to monitor hypermetropia
* Referral for a cardiac review (including echo and ECG) to monitor heart conditions
* Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to monitor spinal and hip issues
* Monitor growth velocity and consider referral for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support development and manage seizures.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets tired more quickly than other kids, even after just playing for a little while, which may indicate a potential cardiac issue.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a feeding aversion, with certain foods not agreeing with him, and mealtime can be challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia (low muscle tone), which affects his movements and balance, and he is working on exercises to help strengthen his muscles.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, of varying types, which typically respond to the usual anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient gets frustrated when there's too much noise around him, and his hearing seems fine otherwise.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient squints quite a bit, which is concerning as it might affect his ability to learn and interact with others.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth break or chip easily, and he needs to be careful with what he eats and make sure he brushes them just right.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Weak enamel is frequently seen in people with KBG syndrome, and careful brushing is very important.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, and most go to a mainstream primary school, but may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has undescended testes, and his movement is a bit different from his friends.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have an unusual structure of their spinal bones, which can give rise to an increased curvature of the spine, and many have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th fingers.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth health and prevent breakage or chipping.
* Regular hearing reviews to age 5 to monitor for conductive hearing loss.
* Eyesight review to monitor for vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long sightedness, and squint.
* Check position of testes in boys and consider referral for further evaluation and treatment if necessary.
* Consider a cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor for heart conditions.
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support the patient's development and address any challenges.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Our daughter has hypermetropia, which means she has a higher-than-normal curvature of her cornea. This affects her ability to see distant objects clearly and requires constant monitoring and corrective measures to prevent further complications. We've been working closely with her ophthalmologist to manage this condition effectively.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Yes, our child often asks people to repeat themselves because she can't seem to catch everything the first time. It's not that she can't hear, but rather that she struggles with processing auditory information quickly. This has led to some frustrations in communication, especially in noisy environments where it's harder for her to focus.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Chewing harder foods has proven challenging for our daughter due to some dental issues we're still trying to fully understand. Her dentist thinks it might be related to the alignment of her teeth or possibly an issue with her jaw. We're exploring orthodontic options to address these difficulties and make eating easier for her.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Physical activities that last for extended periods are particularly taxing for our daughter. She tires easily and can't keep up with her peers during playtime or sports. Cardiologists have noted some concerns regarding her heart's efficiency in pumping blood under stress or exertion. We're managing this with regular exercise tailored to her needs and close supervision from healthcare professionals.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: Developmentally, our daughter reached milestones such as walking and sitting at a slower pace than expected. There was a noticeable delay in these achievements compared to what's typically observed in children of the same age group. Early intervention and support from neurologists and therapists have been invaluable in helping her bridge these gaps.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Weight gain has been slower for our daughter compared to her peers. Despite adequate nutrition and calorie intake, she doesn't seem to put on weight as would be expected. Gastroenterologists have been monitoring her digestive health closely to identify any potential issues that could be contributing to this slow weight gain.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: Language development in our daughter has also been somewhat delayed. At her age, most children are engaging in simple conversations and using a variety of vocabulary. However, our daughter's speech is less advanced. Speech therapists are working with her to enhance her communication skills and encourage more verbal interaction.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has challenges gaining weight at the same rate as her peers, and her parents are exploring ways to support her nutritionally.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has had issues with fluid in her ears, causing discomfort and affecting her hearing at times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has myopia, which affects her ability to engage in class and play with others due to frustration from not being able to see things clearly.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient was born with hip dysplasia, which requires regular monitoring and physical therapy.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient had a glue ear, which caused temporary hearing issues, and is prone to recurrence.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome experience recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has astigmatism, which affects his ability to see clearly unless objects are close up, and requires glasses and exercises to correct it.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, especially to cold foods and drinks, and has had issues that required special toothpaste and gentle brushing.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Individuals with KBG syndrome often have weak enamel, large front teeth, and other dental concerns, making regular dental check-ups important.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient's speech development is a concern, with potential delays or difficulties in conversation and finding the right words.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has coordination and balance issues, which may impact his development and behavior.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety, and may require medication or therapy.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a septal defect that is being monitored closely by a cardiologist to ensure it does not affect daily life significantly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: According to the clinical reference guidelines, around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes, some of which may require surgery or monitoring.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulties with feeding, having challenges with eating certain foods and textures, leading to frustrating meal times.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds. A lack of interest in feeding can be significant and long-lasting.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures occasionally, which are managed closely with a neurologist to reduce their frequency.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome are reported to have seizures, which typically respond to usual anti-epileptic treatments, though in a small number of cases, epilepsy can be difficult to treat.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint and experiences hearing difficulties, often needing people to repeat themselves, especially in noisy places.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, leading to conductive hearing loss. Many children require multiple grommet insertions or hearing aids. Speech delay is common and may be linked to hearing concerns.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a squint that affects his vision, making it hard for him to see things clearly.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint. Treatment can include patching, exercises, glasses, and surgery.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel on his teeth, requiring regular and proper brushing to prevent further problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Besides large front teeth, there can be a variety of other dental concerns, including weak enamel, which is frequently seen in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient is behind in overall developmental progress, which is being monitored with the help of therapists and doctors.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school. Most go to mainstream primary school, but the extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, leading to special schooling or Educational Health Care Plans.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences developmental delays and has overall developmental progress that is being closely monitored.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder, ADHD, or anxiety. Developmental delay is common, ranging from mild to severe, and there is a wide range of eventual ability.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

* Regular dental check-ups to monitor and manage weak enamel.
* Regular hearing reviews, especially in noisy environments, to address hearing difficulties.
* Ophthalmology review to monitor and treat vision problems, including squint.
* Cardiac review to monitor the septal defect and adjust treatment as necessary.
* Neurological monitoring to manage and reduce the frequency of seizures.
* Consideration of physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioural therapy to support developmental delays and behavioural differences.
* Regular monitoring of growth velocity, with consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
* Monitoring for signs of tethered cord, especially if sacral dimple is present or if there are concerns about pain, weakness in the legs, urinary and bowel issues, or an unusual gait.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an abnormal heart valve, which may require monitoring or treatment.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Approximately 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences feeding difficulties and mealtime challenges, with a lack of interest in eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has epilepsy and experiences seizures, which are managed with medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, which typically respond to anti-epileptic treatments.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient may have hearing difficulties, as evidenced by not responding when called, and has required medical attention for ear-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: A significant proportion of people with KBG syndrome have recurrent otitis media or glue ear, which can cause conductive hearing loss.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits squinting behavior, suggesting potential vision problems.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome are more likely to have vision problems, such as astigmatism, short- or long-sightedness, and squint.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has larger-than-expected front teeth, which may be a characteristic feature of KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have large permanent upper middle teeth (macrodontia of upper central incisors) and other dental concerns, such as weak enamel.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences speech delay, which affects communication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require extra help in school, and many have speech delay, which may be linked to hearing concerns.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than expected and is working with therapists to address speech delay and other developmental challenges.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: People with KBG syndrome often have developmental delay, behavioral differences, and may require extra support in school.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has shorter fingers than expected, which may be a characteristic feature of KBG syndrome.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Some people with KBG syndrome have skeletal anomalies, such as short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly), and may experience delayed closure of the soft spot on their head.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
* Regular dental check-ups to monitor tooth development and address any dental concerns
* Regular hearing reviews to assess and address any hearing difficulties
* Eyesight (ophthalmology) review to evaluate and treat any vision problems
* Cardiac review, including echo and ECG, to monitor heart health
* Consideration of a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) to assess bone age and detect any skeletal anomalies
* Monitoring of growth velocity and consideration of endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile
* Physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy to support developmental needs
* Regular monitoring for seizures and adjustment of medication as needed to manage epilepsy
